text: { "entries"   : [  {  "name_han"  :  "無上三元鎮宅靈籙"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "This text proves that domestic misfortune is not random fate but a jurisdictional failure of the Three Primes to seal the dwelling’s boundary against invasive qi. Ritual registration of the house under celestial authority therefore converts an open spatial system into a legally protected domain, so calamity loses its right of entry."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "Premise: dwellings exist at the interface of human, terrestrial, and spectral forces. → Inference: unregistered space is legally vacant and thus claimable by disruptive agents. → Inference: the Three Primes hold the higher charter to assign residence rights. → Inference: a linglu (spirit register) is a binding transfer of jurisdiction, not mere prayer. → Conclusion: once the register is installed and periodically renewed, misfortune is redefined as trespass and can be expelled by the same celestial law that now owns the space."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1) In BaZi house timing, treat years of clashing Earth branches (e.g. year vs. house sitting) as ‘open boundary’ years requiring re-registration rather than only relocation. 2) Map the Three Primes (Upper/Middle/Lower) onto year/month/day officer layers when choosing a 鎮宅 day. 3) Use the occupant’s Day Master and Tai Sui relationship to decide which register layer must lead. 4) After ritual, monitor sickness/finance clusters as evidence of residual unsealed sectors (often Ghost Gate or missing corners). 5) Treat renovation or long vacancy as nullifying prior seal—reapply logic of vacant jurisdiction."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike general 鎮宅符 or 安宅經 that emphasize talismanic force or generic pacification, this text’s core proof is legal-jurisdictional: the linglu is a title deed under San Yuan authority. It differs from pure fengshui form school (which blames terrain) by locating the decisive cause in celestial registration status, so practice is periodic charter renewal rather than permanent architectural fix."  }  ,  {  "name_han"  :  "易林"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "Yi Lin proves that oracular meaning is generated by combinatorial expansion of the sixty-four hexagrams into 4,096 nested situations, each with a fixed poetic outcome-template. Prediction is therefore not free inspiration but retrieval of a pre-encoded case from a closed logical lattice of change."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "Premise: each hexagram already encodes a complete pattern of tendency. → Inference: stacking a second hexagram multiplies contexts without inventing new elemental laws. → Inference: the verse attached to each pair is a compressed case-judgment, not allegory for free association. → Inference: the querent’s question only selects which cell of the lattice is active. → Conclusion: accurate divination equals correct indexing into the combinatorial grid plus disciplined reading of the fixed judgment, not psychic invention."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1) When BaZi shows a clash/combination cluster, map it to a hexagram pair (e.g. stem clash + branch combo) and consult the corresponding Yi Lin judgment as a ‘case precedent.’ 2) Use the outer hexagram for environmental structure and the inner for the native’s agency. 3) Treat repeated draws of the same pair across years as a locked life-theme requiring structural change, not re-asking. 4) In cultivation timing, prefer days whose hexagram pair’s verse favors ‘stillness’ or ‘advance’ before launching retreats. 5) Train against paraphrasing: quote the lattice outcome first, then map to modern facts."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike the Zhou Yi text alone (64 judgments) or later Yarrow/coin methods that stop at one hexagram plus changing lines, Yi Lin proves density of coverage by double-hexagram expansion. It differs from BaZi’s ten-god narrative logic by being a discrete case-library rather than continuous five-phase calculus; the ‘why’ of difference is archival completeness versus dynamic interaction modeling."  }  ,  {  "name_han"  :  "太上玄靈斗姆大聖元君本命延生心經"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "This scripture proves that lifespan and natal fortune are not sealed solely by the birth chart but remain reversible through alignment with Dou Mu, the generative mother of the Dipper stars that administrate destinies. Recitation and mind-seal of the Heart Sutra form operate as a vertical appeal that rewrites the Dipper’s ledger for one’s benming."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "Premise: the Northern Dipper and its mother oversee birth registers and death summons. → Inference: benming (natal destiny) is an administrative file, not an immutable physical law. → Inference: Dou Mu, as source of the Dipper lords, outranks ordinary fate officers. → Inference: heart-sutra form (concise, repetitive, mind-unified) is the protocol for filing a higher appeal. → Conclusion: sincere recitation plus ethical realignment can extend life and soften natal afflictions by changing the file at its source."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1) Identify the native’s 本命星 / natal Dipper correspondence from birth year and schedule Dou Mu practice on that star’s officer day. 2) In BaZi, treat severe ‘hurt officer / seven killings’ lifespan patterns as Dipper-ledger stress—pair chart remedy with Dou Mu heart-sutra cycles rather than only elemental cures. 3) Use the scripture’s 延生 logic when Tai Sui or natal year pillar is in void/emptiness: petition continuity of qi. 4) Combine breath-count recitation with visualizing the Dipper covering the Day Master. 5) Measure results by sleep, acute illness frequency, and ‘near-miss’ event density over 49–100 day courses."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike general 北斗延生經 or star-lord petitions that address individual Dipper officers, this text’s thesis centers Dou Mu as maternal root—appeal goes to the generator of destiny-stars, not the clerks. It differs from pure BaZi remedial objects (crystals, colors) by asserting administrative override through contemplative scripture rather than horizontal five-element balancing."  }  ,  {  "name_han"  :  "玉皇宥罪錫福寶懺"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "This repentance liturgy proves that sin and blessing are opposite entries in the Jade Emperor’s court ledger, so confession is not emotional catharsis but a forensic petition that deletes debit and authorizes credit. Merit is unlocked only after the court accepts the plea of guilt and the vow of reform."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "Premise: the Jade Emperor’s bureaucracy records moral and ritual offenses as cosmic debt. → Inference: unacknowledged debt continues to generate obstructed fortune. → Inference: baochan structure (praise → enumerate sins → request pardon → request blessing) is a complete legal motion. → Inference: 宥罪 must logically precede 錫福; blessing without pardon would violate court consistency. → Conclusion: ritual efficacy equals successful case processing in the celestial court, evidenced by relief of blockage after sincere enumeration and amendment."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1) Before major BaZi ‘luck pillar’ transitions, run a full 宥罪 sequence targeting years of known ethical/ritual breach. 2) Map chart ‘punishment, harm, destruction’ among branches to categories of sin enumerated in the chan text. 3) After pardon section, explicitly petition blessings matching weak chart areas (wealth, health, descendants). 4) Keep a written sin-and-amend list so the ritual is forensic, not theatrical. 5) Re-evaluate within one solar term: if same blockages persist, incomplete confession or unbroken habit is the inference."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Compared with 滿願寶懺, this text prioritizes judicial pardon as the gateway to gift; man-yuan emphasizes vow-fulfillment and wish-completion. Unlike Buddhist repentance that stresses mind-nature purity, this Daoist form proves a court-ledger model under Yuhuang—difference is bureaucratic ontology versus soteriological psychology."  }  ,  {  "name_han"  :  "高上玉皇滿願寶懺"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "This liturgy proves that human vows create binding claims on the celestial treasury only when backed by repentance, praise, and completed ritual performance; ‘full wish’ is the court ratifying that the petitioner’s request and merit are commensurate. Unfulfilled desire is treated as incomplete casework, not cosmic cruelty."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "Premise: vows (yuan) are contracts between human intention and divine office. → Inference: a contract fails if either purity of intent or procedural form is missing. → Inference: baochan supplies the missing purity (confession) and form (ordered liturgy). → Inference: 滿願 means the case reaches closure with granted outcome, not endless petitioning. → Conclusion: systematic completion of the repentance-and-vow sequence is the causal means by which wishes graduate from hope to authorized fulfillment."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1) Convert vague BaZi ‘desires’ into one named vow with time bound and ethical constraint before running man-yuan. 2) Use the chart’s Useful God as the content of the vow (e.g. resource for health, output for recognition). 3) Schedule the chan during months that combine with the Day Branch to ‘close’ the petition. 4) After liturgy, perform the mundane counterpart of the vow within the promised window—court logic demands human performance. 5) If multiple wishes compete, sequence them: one closed yuan before the next filing."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike 宥罪錫福寶懺, which proves debit-clearance before credit, man-yuan proves commensurability of vow and merit toward case closure. It differs from free-form prayer or 許願 without chan by insisting on liturgical completeness; the difference exists because Daoist court theology treats half-performed rites as unfiled paperwork."  }  ,  {  "name_han"  :  "太上洞玄靈寶十號功德因緣妙經"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "This Lingbao scripture proves that invoking the Ten Titles of the Dao is not honorific flattery but activation of ten distinct causal merit-channels (gongde yinyuan). Each title names a function; reciting them in order stitches the practitioner into those functions’ salvific network."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "Premise: in Lingbao ontology, true names and titles carry operative power. → Inference: the Ten Titles partition the Dao’s salvific work into discrete offices. → Inference: ‘merit-cause’ means each title is a seed that matures as a specific class of benefit when correctly recited. → Inference: sequence and completeness prevent partial, unbalanced activation. → Conclusion: scripture practice is engineered causality—title → channel → merit—rather than devotional mood alone."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1) Align each of the ten titles with a life domain (protection, teaching, liberation, etc.) and track which domain your BaZi most lacks. 2) During years of void fate or broken combinations, recite full ten-title cycles to re-seed missing causal links. 3) Use the jing as opening liturgy before talisman or jiao work to establish merit-right to act. 4) In cultivation, couple each title with one breath and one bow to embody channel activation. 5) Log synchronic improvements by domain to verify which titles ‘fire’ for your chart."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike pure 步虛 or praise hymns that elevate mind through beauty, this text’s thesis is causal engineering via titled functions. It differs from 三元 or star-lord registers by working through Lingbao name-theology rather than astral bureaucracy; the why is Lingbao’s emphasis on scriptural merit networks over stellar policing."  }  ,  {  "name_han"  :  "太上慈悲九幽拔罪懺"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "This repentance proves that suffering in the Nine Underworlds is structured debt across multiple dark realms, and that compassionate intervention can extract (ba) the guilty only after systematic confession mapped to each layer. Salvation of the dead is thus layered jurisprudence plus mercy, not a single blanket absolution."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "Premise: 九幽 names a stratified geography of postmortem obstruction. → Inference: sins and attachments lodge at different layers; one generic apology cannot clear all. → Inference: chan text that walks layer by layer is a full audit. → Inference: 慈悲 is the authorizing motive that lets the living file on behalf of the dead. → Conclusion: successful 拔罪 requires complete layered confession + transfer of merit + intention of compassion, producing release rather than temporary comfort."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1) For ancestral BaZi patterns that repeat (same clash killing lineage), treat as unfinished underworld debt and schedule jiu-you chan. 2) Match illness types or family ‘curse-like’ themes to specific you-layers enumerated in the text. 3) Offer merit from the living’s good deeds and chart-strong years as transfer capital. 4) Perform on Zhongyuan or descending days when underworld gates are ritually accessible. 5) After rites, watch for dream release, reduced household accidents, and softening of inherited chart patterns in the next generation’s luck."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike 玉皇宥罪 chan aimed at the living petitioner’s court file, this text targets the dead across Nine You—vertical underworld geography versus heavenly court ledger. It differs from simple 超度 food offerings by proving forensic layer-by-layer extraction; the difference is completeness of dark-realm jurisprudence under Lingbao compassion ideology."  }  ,  {  "name_han"  :  "高上神霄宗師受經式"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "This text proves that Shenxiao scriptural power is illegitimate without formal transmission ritual: the 受經式 is the legal induction that binds disciple, master, and thunder-department authority. Without the rite, possession of the text is theft of celestial office, so talismans will not marshal thunder generals."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "Premise: Shenxiao rites command martial spirit bureaucracies that only obey credentialed officers. → Inference: scripture is both manual and badge of office. → Inference: 受經式 publicly and cosmically installs the badge. → Inference: skipped transmission creates a gap between knowledge and authority. → Conclusion: efficacy of thunder rites depends on verified lineage reception, not merely correct reading of instructions."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1) Before practicing any Shenxiao-derived 雷法 or related BaZi ‘killing qi’ subjugation rites, verify transmission status—if absent, restrict to devotional reading. 2) Treat 受經 day as a personal ‘officer appointment’ date; record it like a luck-pillar start. 3) Align reception timing with strong Day Master or supportive Resource months so the ‘badge’ seats in robust qi. 4) After reception, keep precepts listed in the式 as operational constraints on spell use. 5) In teaching, refuse to transmit technique without the式—preserve causal link of authority."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike public 心經 or 懺 texts meant for open recitation, this is a meta-ritual about who may wield scripture. It differs from general 傳度 or ordination manuals by specifying Shenxiao thunder lineage logic—authority is martial-bureaucratic. The why: thunder magic without badge is treated as impersonating an officer of the Divine Empyrean."  }  ,  {  "name_han"  :  "玄和子十二月卦金訣"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "This work proves that the twelve monthly hexagrams (message of waxing/waning yang) are a golden operational key for timing alchemy and action: microcosmic fire phases must lock to macrocosmic month-gua, or effort fights the season’s vector."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "Premise: from 復 to 姤 and the twelve sovereign hexagrams, yang’s rise and fall are calendrically fixed. → Inference: human qi and medicinal fire are smaller instances of the same pattern. → Inference: ‘gold key’ means compressed rules that translate each month-gua into do/don’t for cultivation. → Inference: working against the month-gua wastes jing/qi or scatters the medicine. → Conclusion: correct practice is synchronous: choose techniques and intensities that match the month’s hexagram vector."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1) Overlay the twelve month gua on the BaZi annual/monthly branches (e.g. midwinter 復 = Zi month) when planning retreats. 2) Increase collecting practices in yang-rising months (丑–巳 direction of the cycle) and emphasize storing/protecting in yang-falling months. 3) For chart holders with weak yang Day Masters, never force peak fire work in 剝/坤 seasonal phases. 4) Use the金訣 maxims as checklists before opening the furnace (literal or physiological). 5) Journal month-gua vs. body signs (cold/heat, libido, clarity) to personalize the key."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike raw Yijing monthly gua lists or general 節氣 health advice, this text claims a ‘golden key’—operative compression for neidan/waidan timing. It differs from pure BaZi ten-god monthly luck by using hexagram vectors of pure yang measure rather than stem-branch social/functional gods; the why is alchemical isomorphism of cosmos and furnace."  }  ,  {  "name_han"  :  "石藥爾雅"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "Shi Yao Er Ya proves that alchemical failure often comes from nominal chaos: the same mineral has many names, and misidentification breaks causal chains of formula. Lexicographic standardization is therefore a safety and efficacy logic, not scholastic pedantry."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "Premise: external alchemy depends on exact substance properties. → Inference: traders and traditions multiply alternate names. → Inference: without a synonym lexicon, the practitioner cannot guarantee isomorphic ingredients. → Inference: wrong stone yields wrong reaction, toxicity, or null elixir. → Conclusion: true mastery begins with name-to-substance mapping; dictionary work is part of the Dao of medicine."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1) When reading classical 丹方, cross-check every mineral alias against Shi Yao Er Ya before any modern analogue experiment (or treat as historical only if toxic). 2) Build a personal glossary linking traditional names → modern mineral IDs → toxicity class. 3) Apply the same logic to BaZi ‘herbal/mineral cures’: refuse unnamed ‘magic sand’ remedies. 4) In textual study, treat variant drug names as a source of lineage disagreement, not deeper mysticism. 5) Prefer formulas whose ingredients survive synonym collapse to a consistent set."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike 丹方鑑源 (provenance of recipes) or 大丹記 (process narrative), this is a philological-instrumental proof: language hygiene as alchemical method. It differs from Bencao materia medica by focusing on elixir stones and their secret names; the why is the cryptonymic culture of waidan transmission."  }  ,  {  "name_han"  :  "丹方鑑源"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "Dan Fang Jian Yuan proves that elixir formulas must be sourced and authenticated—‘mirroring the source’—because spurious recipes circulate with prestige titles. Discriminating origin is the logical filter that separates operative methods from literary forgeries."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "Premise: the market and manuscript tradition mix genuine and false danfang. → Inference: identical titles can hide divergent ingredients and fire regimes. → Inference: tracing 源 (source/lineage) is the only non-experimental test before risking life. → Inference: ‘mirror’ implies comparative inspection across versions. → Conclusion: critical bibliography is a stage of alchemy; unexamined formulas are not yet knowledge."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1) For any cultivation recipe (herb, mineral, or ‘spiritual fire’ metaphor), demand lineage and earliest attestation. 2) Cross-read at least two independent witnesses before practice. 3) In BaZi remedial culture, reject one-off internet ‘elixirs’ lacking source chain. 4) Rank methods by transparency of process variables (times, signs, stop conditions). 5) Keep a rejected-formula list to prevent cyclic rediscovery of known dross."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Compared with 石藥爾雅 (what the substance is called) and 大丹記 (how a great elixir proceeds), Jian Yuan answers ‘which text is trustworthy.’ It differs from hagiographic 神仙傳 by applying critical sourcing rather than faith in miracle stories; the why is risk control in a literature flooded with pseudepigrapha."  }  ,  {  "name_han"  :  "大丹記"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "Da Dan Ji proves that the Great Elixir is a staged transformational sequence with observable phase-signs; success is recognized by correct transitions, not by duration alone. The record functions as a causal log: ingredients, fire, times, and endpoints form a reproducible argument."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "Premise: great elixir claims must be more than metaphor if they guide practice. → Inference: a 記 (record) structures process into ordered phases. → Inference: each phase has entry criteria and exit signs. → Inference: skipping phases or misreading signs collapses the product. → Conclusion: cultivation/alchemy is validated by matching lived signs to the recorded phase logic of the Great Elixir."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1) Translate the text’s stages into a checklist for neidan (or historical study for waidan): essence stabilization → qi movement → spirit condensation → resting. 2) Pair stages with BaZi periods: do not force late stages in years of severe Resource drain. 3) Define failure signs (agitation, insomnia, compulsive heat) as phase errors, not ‘tests from demons’ only. 4) Time stage shifts to monthly gua or solar terms per companion alchemical calendars. 5) Write your own 記 after each retreat—make personal causality as explicit as the classic."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike 神仙養生祕術 (plural techniques for nurturing life) or 靈草歌 (herbal songs), Da Dan Ji centers one grand process model. It differs from purely philosophical 悟真篇 poetry by presenting record-like procedural logic; the why is to prove reproducibility of the ‘great’ work through staged evidence."  }  ,  {  "name_han"  :  "神仙養生祕術"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "This text proves that immortality arts are composite: longevity emerges from a toolkit of secret techniques (breath, diet, sexual hygiene, herbs, exercises) coordinated as a system. No single trick substitutes for the full economy of nurturing life."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "Premise: body and spirit leak through multiple pathways. → Inference: each 祕術 patches a pathway (or optimizes a resource). → Inference: isolated practice leaves other leaks open, nullifying gains. → Inference: secrecy marks operational details that determine dose and timing. → Conclusion: true yangsheng is multi-factor control under disciplined sequencing, not one legendary method."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1) Audit your BaZi weak points (Blood/Resource, Officer stress, Output scatter) and assign a matching technique class from the book. 2) Build a daily stack: breath + sleep timing + diet restraint + mild movement. 3) Use ‘secret’ dosing logic—start minimal, increase only with stable pulse/sleep. 4) In sexual and emotional hygiene, treat Seven Killings months as high-leak periods. 5) Reassess quarterly; drop techniques that conflict (e.g. extreme sweating while yin is depleted)."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike 大丹記’s single great-elixir arc, this is a modular secret-arts compendium. It differs from purely meditative 心性 texts by stressing somatic and dietary operations; the why is practical immortality as systems engineering of the living body."  }  ,  {  "name_han"  :  "白雲仙人靈草歌"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "The Spirit Herb Song proves that efficacious plants are knowable through mnemonic verse: morphological marks, habitats, and effects are compressed into song so field identification and use stay linked. Botanical correctitude is the hidden premise of ‘numinous’ results."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "Premise: wrong herb yields wrong or lethal effect. → Inference: oral-song form maximizes memorability for gatherers. → Inference: each stanza pairs appearance with function, encoding a mini argument. → Inference: ‘ling’ quality depends on true species plus right processing, not brand magic. → Conclusion: singing the herb is training the perceptual-logical map that makes spiritual pharmacy reliable."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1) When a BaZi remedy tradition names a grass/root, verify identity via the song’s traits before use. 2) Match herb natures (cold/hot, drying/moist) to chart excess-deficiency, not only to folklore prestige. 3) Use seasonal gathering cues in the verses as timing rules (parallel to month-gua discipline). 4) Prefer single-herb clarity before complex patent formulas. 5) Treat the song as exam material: if you cannot recite marks, you are not ready to dose."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike 石藥爾雅 (mineral names) or abstract 丹經, this is field botany in poetic code. It differs from imperial Bencao encyclopedias by prioritizing portable song-logic for mountain practitioners; the why is operational memory under Baiyun immortal herb tradition rather than desk scholarship."  }  ,  {  "name_han"  :  "金華赤松山志"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "This mountain monograph proves that sacred geography is historical accumulation of adepts, rites, and sites: a mountain becomes ‘gold flower’ immortal terrain because lineage events sediment into landscape. Place is an archive of successful cultivation, not mute scenery."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "Premise: Chisong and related immortals leave traces in named peaks, caves, and shrines. → Inference: recording them as 志 binds story to coordinate. → Inference: later practitioners can navigate both terrain and method by the same map. → Inference: pilgrimage without the zhi is spatial tourism; with it, one enters a curriculum of place. → Conclusion: mountain gazetteers argue that Dao is locally proven—geography authenticates practice."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1) When selecting retreat sites, prefer places with documented immortal lineage over generic ‘pretty mountains.’ 2) Align personal BaZi travel stars and annual direction with the mountain’s historically potent sectors. 3) On-site, practice forms recorded in the zhi rather than imported unrelated systems. 4) Treat local taboos in the text as safety logic (spirit jurisdiction again). 5) After return, note which chart issues eased—build evidence for place-person fit."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike abstract 洞天記 lists, Jin Hua Chisong Shan Zhi is a thick local history of one range. It differs from pure 內傳 hagiography by grounding biography in topography; the why is to prove that cultivation success leaves mappable, revisit-able infrastructure."  }  ,  {  "name_han"  :  "大滌洞天記"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "Da Di Dongtian Ji proves that a Grotto-Heaven is an administrative-spiritual unit with boundaries, officers, and purification functions (‘great cleansing’). Entering it is changing legal-spiritual jurisdiction, which accelerates refinement when the adept respects the cave-heaven’s rules."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "Premise: Daoist cosmography ranks 洞天 as concentrated pure qi zones under specific governance. → Inference: Da Di’s record defines this zone’s identity and rites. → Inference: 滌 implies the locale’s primary causal gift is cleansing of turbidity. → Inference: correct entry timing and conduct open that function; violation closes it. → Conclusion: place-based cultivation works by jurisdictional immersion in a cleansing field, not by scenery psychology alone."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1) Schedule cave-heaven retreats during personal chart turbidity peaks (heavy combo of Direct Officer + Wet Earth, or illness pillars). 2) Observe entry purification from the记 before any ‘advanced’ practice. 3) Use shorter, repeated immersions if Day Master is weak—cleansing can feel draining. 4) Pair with confession chans so moral and qi turbidity clear together. 5) After exit, implement dietary/behavioral seals so re-pollution does not nullify the field effect."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Compared with 赤松山志 (lineage-landscape history) or 王屋山聖跡記 (miracle traces), this text’s thesis is grotto-heaven as cleansing jurisdiction. It differs from generic fengshui ‘qi cave’ talk by embedding official Daoist dongtian administration; the why is canonical sacred geography rather than folk geomancy."  }  ,  {  "name_han"  :  "天壇王屋山聖跡記"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "This record proves Wangwu’s Heavenly Altar as a site where imperial-celestial contact left verifiable ‘holy traces,’ so the mountain functions as a permanent interface for audience with higher powers. Pilgrimage and rite there borrow the residual authority of those traces."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "Premise: 聖跡 are material or narrative marks of successful theophany or immortal activity. → Inference: collecting them into a 記 creates an evidence portfolio for the site’s rank. → Inference: Wangwu as 天壇 implies altar-grade access, not ordinary scenic numen. → Inference: later ritual reenacts or plugs into that access channel. → Conclusion: practicing at Wangwu is argument by continuity—standing where heaven once answered multiplies the probability of response."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1) Reserve Wangwu (or analogous altar mountains) for petitions of rank: lifespan, ordination, major vow closure—not trivial wishes. 2) Read the聖跡 before ascent; ritually greet the specific traces named. 3) Choose years when BaZi Traveling Horse is active and beneficial. 4) Combine with Yuhuang or Shangqing chans that match the mountain’s historical pantheon. 5) Document personal ‘traces’ (events, dreams, recoveries) as continuation of the evidential logic."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike 南嶽小錄’s broader Hengshan miscellany, this focuses on proving altar-grade sanctity via miracle inventory. It differs from 大滌洞天記’s cleansing-grotto thesis by emphasizing hierarchical audience (heaven’s altar) over purgation; the why is Wangwu’s classical status in retirement/immortal ascent lore."  }  ,  {  "name_han"  :  "南嶽小錄"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "Nan Yue Xiao Lu proves that a sacred marchmount is best known through compact, practical notes—temples, peaks, distances, numinous anecdotes—so the adept can orient without drowning in encyclopedism. Small-record form is an epistemology of usable sacred space."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "Premise: Nanyue is vast in cults and terrain. → Inference: without a concise lu, pilgrims misroute energy and time. → Inference: ‘small record’ selects operational facts over exhaustive history. → Inference: selection itself teaches what the tradition deems causally important. → Conclusion: effective mountain practice depends on a portable cognitive map of sites and their functions."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1) Before Nanyue pilgrimage, extract a route of sites matched to your aim (repentance temples vs. cultivation peaks). 2) Use the xiao lu’s scale notes to plan realistic day-qi expenditure for your constitution/chart. 3) At each stop, perform only the function historically noted—avoid ritual sprawl. 4) Compare your BaZi useful directions with the approach axes of major peaks. 5) After return, write your own ‘small record’ to refine future entries."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike long 山志 such as Chisong’s monograph, Xiao Lu prizes brevity and navigability. It differs from 聖跡記 by balancing logistics with lore rather than centering miracle proof; the why is handbook utility for the Southern Marchmount’s complex cult landscape."  }  ,  {  "name_han"  :  "太上玉清謝罪登真寶懺"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "This repentance proves that ascent to Zhen-hood (登真) is blocked by unconfessed faults against the Jade Clarity order; apology is the solvent of those blocks. Thus the path to perfection is not only refining qi but clearing legal-moral charges in the highest pure realm’s court."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "Premise: Yuqing is the apex purity stratum; its standards define true immortal rank. → Inference: offenses create incompatibility with that stratum. → Inference: 謝罪 is formal removal of incompatibility. → Inference: only then does 登真 become a coherent outcome of practice. → Conclusion: baochan links ethics and ontology—without apology, technical cultivation cannot seat in Jade Clarity."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1) Before attempting high neidan ‘spirit projection / immortal embryo’ stages, run full 謝罪 cycles. 2) Inventory faults against teacher, scriptures, body (jing waste), and beings—Yuqing logic is strict. 3) Time the chan in Metal/Water pure months or on your Authority days for solemnity. 4) Pair with silence retreat so apology is not immediately re-violated. 5) Treat recurring cultivation plateaus as possible unconfessed charges; audit again."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Unlike 九幽拔罪 (rescuing beings from dark realms) or 泰清拔罪昇天 (Taiqing ascent after sin extraction), this text ties apology specifically to Yuqing-rank perfection. It differs from 宥罪錫福 (pardon for blessing) by aiming at ontological promotion (登真) rather than worldly fortune; the why is Shangqing/Yuqing soteriology of pure realization."  }  ,  {  "name_han"  :  "太上泰清拔罪昇天寶懺"  ,  "logic_thesis"  :  "This liturgy proves a two-stage causal law: extraction of sin (拔罪) must complete before heavenly ascent (昇天) can be authorized under the Taiqing dispensation. Ascent is not escape from judgment but the positive sequel of a cleared record."  ,  "logic_chain"  :  "Premise: Taiqing governance handles salvation and aerial promotion of souls/practitioners. → Inference: residual guilt has weight that prevents rising. → Inference: chan systematically pulls out guilt (拔) rather than merely covering it. → Inference: 昇天 is the consequent state once weight is gone. → Conclusion: the ritual’s sequence is the argument—clear first, rise second—binding moral physics to celestial mobility."  ,  "logic_practice"  :  "1) Use for death anniversaries and for living practitioners stuck in ‘heavy’ chart years (strong Tomb storage, multiple punishments). 2) Never skip the 拔罪 half to rush ‘ascent’ visualizations—sequence is causal. 3) In BaZi terms, treat this as converting Killing/Officer pressure into pure Output rise only after confession. 4) Combine with merit transfer and precept renewal as ballast removal. 5) Indicators of success: lightness of mood-body, resolved nightmares, and opportunistic openings in career/cultivation path within weeks."  ,  "logic_compare"  :  "Compared with 玉清謝罪登真, which emphasizes apology toward perfection in Jade Clarity, Taiqing 拔罪昇天 stresses extraction plus vertical lift under Taiqing. It differs from 九幽拔罪 by aiming upward to heaven rather than primarily liberating from underworld layers; the why is distinct bureaucratic heavens (Taiqing vs Yuqing vs Jiuyou) with different end-states: flight, zhen-hood, or underworld release."  }  ]  }
thought: The user wants me to extract logical reasoning from 20 classical Daoist/BaZi related texts and return structured JSON. Let me research these texts to provide accurate scholarly analysis rather than gu...

entries.logic_thesis: This text proves that domestic misfortune is not random fate but a jurisdictional failure of the Three Primes to seal the dwelling’s boundary against invasive qi. Ritual registration of the house under celestial authority therefore converts an open spatial system into a legally protected domain, so calamity loses its right of entry.
entries.logic_chain: Premise: dwellings exist at the interface of human, terrestrial, and spectral forces. → Inference: unregistered space is legally vacant and thus claimable by disruptive agents. → Inference: the Three Primes hold the higher charter to assign residence rights. → Inference: a linglu (spirit register) is a binding transfer of jurisdiction, not mere prayer. → Conclusion: once the register is installed and periodically renewed, misfortune is redefined as trespass and can be expelled by the same celestial law that now owns the space.
entries.logic_practice: 1) In BaZi house timing, treat years of clashing Earth branches (e.g. year vs. house sitting) as ‘open boundary’ years requiring re-registration rather than only relocation. 2) Map the Three Primes (Upper/Middle/Lower) onto year/month/day officer layers when choosing a 鎮宅 day. 3) Use the occupant’s Day Master and Tai Sui relationship to decide which register layer must lead. 4) After ritual, monitor sickness/finance clusters as evidence of residual unsealed sectors (often Ghost Gate or missing corners). 5) Treat renovation or long vacancy as nullifying prior seal—reapply logic of vacant jurisdiction.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike general 鎮宅符 or 安宅經 that emphasize talismanic force or generic pacification, this text’s core proof is legal-jurisdictional: the linglu is a title deed under San Yuan authority. It differs from pure fengshui form school (which blames terrain) by locating the decisive cause in celestial registration status, so practice is periodic charter renewal rather than permanent architectural fix.

entries.logic_thesis: Yi Lin proves that oracular meaning is generated by combinatorial expansion of the sixty-four hexagrams into 4,096 nested situations, each with a fixed poetic outcome-template. Prediction is therefore not free inspiration but retrieval of a pre-encoded case from a closed logical lattice of change.
entries.logic_chain: Premise: each hexagram already encodes a complete pattern of tendency. → Inference: stacking a second hexagram multiplies contexts without inventing new elemental laws. → Inference: the verse attached to each pair is a compressed case-judgment, not allegory for free association. → Inference: the querent’s question only selects which cell of the lattice is active. → Conclusion: accurate divination equals correct indexing into the combinatorial grid plus disciplined reading of the fixed judgment, not psychic invention.
entries.logic_practice: 1) When BaZi shows a clash/combination cluster, map it to a hexagram pair (e.g. stem clash + branch combo) and consult the corresponding Yi Lin judgment as a ‘case precedent.’ 2) Use the outer hexagram for environmental structure and the inner for the native’s agency. 3) Treat repeated draws of the same pair across years as a locked life-theme requiring structural change, not re-asking. 4) In cultivation timing, prefer days whose hexagram pair’s verse favors ‘stillness’ or ‘advance’ before launching retreats. 5) Train against paraphrasing: quote the lattice outcome first, then map to modern facts.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike the Zhou Yi text alone (64 judgments) or later Yarrow/coin methods that stop at one hexagram plus changing lines, Yi Lin proves density of coverage by double-hexagram expansion. It differs from BaZi’s ten-god narrative logic by being a discrete case-library rather than continuous five-phase calculus; the ‘why’ of difference is archival completeness versus dynamic interaction modeling.

entries.name_han: 太上玄靈斗姆大聖元君本命延生心經
entries.logic_thesis: This scripture proves that lifespan and natal fortune are not sealed solely by the birth chart but remain reversible through alignment with Dou Mu, the generative mother of the Dipper stars that administrate destinies. Recitation and mind-seal of the Heart Sutra form operate as a vertical appeal that rewrites the Dipper’s ledger for one’s benming.
entries.logic_chain: Premise: the Northern Dipper and its mother oversee birth registers and death summons. → Inference: benming (natal destiny) is an administrative file, not an immutable physical law. → Inference: Dou Mu, as source of the Dipper lords, outranks ordinary fate officers. → Inference: heart-sutra form (concise, repetitive, mind-unified) is the protocol for filing a higher appeal. → Conclusion: sincere recitation plus ethical realignment can extend life and soften natal afflictions by changing the file at its source.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Identify the native’s 本命星 / natal Dipper correspondence from birth year and schedule Dou Mu practice on that star’s officer day. 2) In BaZi, treat severe ‘hurt officer / seven killings’ lifespan patterns as Dipper-ledger stress—pair chart remedy with Dou Mu heart-sutra cycles rather than only elemental cures. 3) Use the scripture’s 延生 logic when Tai Sui or natal year pillar is in void/emptiness: petition continuity of qi. 4) Combine breath-count recitation with visualizing the Dipper covering the Day Master. 5) Measure results by sleep, acute illness frequency, and ‘near-miss’ event density over 49–100 day courses.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike general 北斗延生經 or star-lord petitions that address individual Dipper officers, this text’s thesis centers Dou Mu as maternal root—appeal goes to the generator of destiny-stars, not the clerks. It differs from pure BaZi remedial objects (crystals, colors) by asserting administrative override through contemplative scripture rather than horizontal five-element balancing.

entries.logic_thesis: This repentance liturgy proves that sin and blessing are opposite entries in the Jade Emperor’s court ledger, so confession is not emotional catharsis but a forensic petition that deletes debit and authorizes credit. Merit is unlocked only after the court accepts the plea of guilt and the vow of reform.
entries.logic_chain: Premise: the Jade Emperor’s bureaucracy records moral and ritual offenses as cosmic debt. → Inference: unacknowledged debt continues to generate obstructed fortune. → Inference: baochan structure (praise → enumerate sins → request pardon → request blessing) is a complete legal motion. → Inference: 宥罪 must logically precede 錫福; blessing without pardon would violate court consistency. → Conclusion: ritual efficacy equals successful case processing in the celestial court, evidenced by relief of blockage after sincere enumeration and amendment.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Before major BaZi ‘luck pillar’ transitions, run a full 宥罪 sequence targeting years of known ethical/ritual breach. 2) Map chart ‘punishment, harm, destruction’ among branches to categories of sin enumerated in the chan text. 3) After pardon section, explicitly petition blessings matching weak chart areas (wealth, health, descendants). 4) Keep a written sin-and-amend list so the ritual is forensic, not theatrical. 5) Re-evaluate within one solar term: if same blockages persist, incomplete confession or unbroken habit is the inference.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with 滿願寶懺, this text prioritizes judicial pardon as the gateway to gift; man-yuan emphasizes vow-fulfillment and wish-completion. Unlike Buddhist repentance that stresses mind-nature purity, this Daoist form proves a court-ledger model under Yuhuang—difference is bureaucratic ontology versus soteriological psychology.

entries.logic_thesis: This liturgy proves that human vows create binding claims on the celestial treasury only when backed by repentance, praise, and completed ritual performance; ‘full wish’ is the court ratifying that the petitioner’s request and merit are commensurate. Unfulfilled desire is treated as incomplete casework, not cosmic cruelty.
entries.logic_chain: Premise: vows (yuan) are contracts between human intention and divine office. → Inference: a contract fails if either purity of intent or procedural form is missing. → Inference: baochan supplies the missing purity (confession) and form (ordered liturgy). → Inference: 滿願 means the case reaches closure with granted outcome, not endless petitioning. → Conclusion: systematic completion of the repentance-and-vow sequence is the causal means by which wishes graduate from hope to authorized fulfillment.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Convert vague BaZi ‘desires’ into one named vow with time bound and ethical constraint before running man-yuan. 2) Use the chart’s Useful God as the content of the vow (e.g. resource for health, output for recognition). 3) Schedule the chan during months that combine with the Day Branch to ‘close’ the petition. 4) After liturgy, perform the mundane counterpart of the vow within the promised window—court logic demands human performance. 5) If multiple wishes compete, sequence them: one closed yuan before the next filing.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 宥罪錫福寶懺, which proves debit-clearance before credit, man-yuan proves commensurability of vow and merit toward case closure. It differs from free-form prayer or 許願 without chan by insisting on liturgical completeness; the difference exists because Daoist court theology treats half-performed rites as unfiled paperwork.

entries.name_han: 太上洞玄靈寶十號功德因緣妙經
entries.logic_thesis: This Lingbao scripture proves that invoking the Ten Titles of the Dao is not honorific flattery but activation of ten distinct causal merit-channels (gongde yinyuan). Each title names a function; reciting them in order stitches the practitioner into those functions’ salvific network.
entries.logic_chain: Premise: in Lingbao ontology, true names and titles carry operative power. → Inference: the Ten Titles partition the Dao’s salvific work into discrete offices. → Inference: ‘merit-cause’ means each title is a seed that matures as a specific class of benefit when correctly recited. → Inference: sequence and completeness prevent partial, unbalanced activation. → Conclusion: scripture practice is engineered causality—title → channel → merit—rather than devotional mood alone.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Align each of the ten titles with a life domain (protection, teaching, liberation, etc.) and track which domain your BaZi most lacks. 2) During years of void fate or broken combinations, recite full ten-title cycles to re-seed missing causal links. 3) Use the jing as opening liturgy before talisman or jiao work to establish merit-right to act. 4) In cultivation, couple each title with one breath and one bow to embody channel activation. 5) Log synchronic improvements by domain to verify which titles ‘fire’ for your chart.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike pure 步虛 or praise hymns that elevate mind through beauty, this text’s thesis is causal engineering via titled functions. It differs from 三元 or star-lord registers by working through Lingbao name-theology rather than astral bureaucracy; the why is Lingbao’s emphasis on scriptural merit networks over stellar policing.

entries.logic_thesis: This repentance proves that suffering in the Nine Underworlds is structured debt across multiple dark realms, and that compassionate intervention can extract (ba) the guilty only after systematic confession mapped to each layer. Salvation of the dead is thus layered jurisprudence plus mercy, not a single blanket absolution.
entries.logic_chain: Premise: 九幽 names a stratified geography of postmortem obstruction. → Inference: sins and attachments lodge at different layers; one generic apology cannot clear all. → Inference: chan text that walks layer by layer is a full audit. → Inference: 慈悲 is the authorizing motive that lets the living file on behalf of the dead. → Conclusion: successful 拔罪 requires complete layered confession + transfer of merit + intention of compassion, producing release rather than temporary comfort.
entries.logic_practice: 1) For ancestral BaZi patterns that repeat (same clash killing lineage), treat as unfinished underworld debt and schedule jiu-you chan. 2) Match illness types or family ‘curse-like’ themes to specific you-layers enumerated in the text. 3) Offer merit from the living’s good deeds and chart-strong years as transfer capital. 4) Perform on Zhongyuan or descending days when underworld gates are ritually accessible. 5) After rites, watch for dream release, reduced household accidents, and softening of inherited chart patterns in the next generation’s luck.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 玉皇宥罪 chan aimed at the living petitioner’s court file, this text targets the dead across Nine You—vertical underworld geography versus heavenly court ledger. It differs from simple 超度 food offerings by proving forensic layer-by-layer extraction; the difference is completeness of dark-realm jurisprudence under Lingbao compassion ideology.

entries.logic_thesis: This text proves that Shenxiao scriptural power is illegitimate without formal transmission ritual: the 受經式 is the legal induction that binds disciple, master, and thunder-department authority. Without the rite, possession of the text is theft of celestial office, so talismans will not marshal thunder generals.
entries.logic_chain: Premise: Shenxiao rites command martial spirit bureaucracies that only obey credentialed officers. → Inference: scripture is both manual and badge of office. → Inference: 受經式 publicly and cosmically installs the badge. → Inference: skipped transmission creates a gap between knowledge and authority. → Conclusion: efficacy of thunder rites depends on verified lineage reception, not merely correct reading of instructions.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Before practicing any Shenxiao-derived 雷法 or related BaZi ‘killing qi’ subjugation rites, verify transmission status—if absent, restrict to devotional reading. 2) Treat 受經 day as a personal ‘officer appointment’ date; record it like a luck-pillar start. 3) Align reception timing with strong Day Master or supportive Resource months so the ‘badge’ seats in robust qi. 4) After reception, keep precepts listed in the式 as operational constraints on spell use. 5) In teaching, refuse to transmit technique without the式—preserve causal link of authority.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike public 心經 or 懺 texts meant for open recitation, this is a meta-ritual about who may wield scripture. It differs from general 傳度 or ordination manuals by specifying Shenxiao thunder lineage logic—authority is martial-bureaucratic. The why: thunder magic without badge is treated as impersonating an officer of the Divine Empyrean.

entries.logic_thesis: This work proves that the twelve monthly hexagrams (message of waxing/waning yang) are a golden operational key for timing alchemy and action: microcosmic fire phases must lock to macrocosmic month-gua, or effort fights the season’s vector.
entries.logic_chain: Premise: from 復 to 姤 and the twelve sovereign hexagrams, yang’s rise and fall are calendrically fixed. → Inference: human qi and medicinal fire are smaller instances of the same pattern. → Inference: ‘gold key’ means compressed rules that translate each month-gua into do/don’t for cultivation. → Inference: working against the month-gua wastes jing/qi or scatters the medicine. → Conclusion: correct practice is synchronous: choose techniques and intensities that match the month’s hexagram vector.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Overlay the twelve month gua on the BaZi annual/monthly branches (e.g. midwinter 復 = Zi month) when planning retreats. 2) Increase collecting practices in yang-rising months (丑–巳 direction of the cycle) and emphasize storing/protecting in yang-falling months. 3) For chart holders with weak yang Day Masters, never force peak fire work in 剝/坤 seasonal phases. 4) Use the金訣 maxims as checklists before opening the furnace (literal or physiological). 5) Journal month-gua vs. body signs (cold/heat, libido, clarity) to personalize the key.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike raw Yijing monthly gua lists or general 節氣 health advice, this text claims a ‘golden key’—operative compression for neidan/waidan timing. It differs from pure BaZi ten-god monthly luck by using hexagram vectors of pure yang measure rather than stem-branch social/functional gods; the why is alchemical isomorphism of cosmos and furnace.

entries.logic_thesis: Shi Yao Er Ya proves that alchemical failure often comes from nominal chaos: the same mineral has many names, and misidentification breaks causal chains of formula. Lexicographic standardization is therefore a safety and efficacy logic, not scholastic pedantry.
entries.logic_chain: Premise: external alchemy depends on exact substance properties. → Inference: traders and traditions multiply alternate names. → Inference: without a synonym lexicon, the practitioner cannot guarantee isomorphic ingredients. → Inference: wrong stone yields wrong reaction, toxicity, or null elixir. → Conclusion: true mastery begins with name-to-substance mapping; dictionary work is part of the Dao of medicine.
entries.logic_practice: 1) When reading classical 丹方, cross-check every mineral alias against Shi Yao Er Ya before any modern analogue experiment (or treat as historical only if toxic). 2) Build a personal glossary linking traditional names → modern mineral IDs → toxicity class. 3) Apply the same logic to BaZi ‘herbal/mineral cures’: refuse unnamed ‘magic sand’ remedies. 4) In textual study, treat variant drug names as a source of lineage disagreement, not deeper mysticism. 5) Prefer formulas whose ingredients survive synonym collapse to a consistent set.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 丹方鑑源 (provenance of recipes) or 大丹記 (process narrative), this is a philological-instrumental proof: language hygiene as alchemical method. It differs from Bencao materia medica by focusing on elixir stones and their secret names; the why is the cryptonymic culture of waidan transmission.

entries.logic_thesis: Dan Fang Jian Yuan proves that elixir formulas must be sourced and authenticated—‘mirroring the source’—because spurious recipes circulate with prestige titles. Discriminating origin is the logical filter that separates operative methods from literary forgeries.
entries.logic_chain: Premise: the market and manuscript tradition mix genuine and false danfang. → Inference: identical titles can hide divergent ingredients and fire regimes. → Inference: tracing 源 (source/lineage) is the only non-experimental test before risking life. → Inference: ‘mirror’ implies comparative inspection across versions. → Conclusion: critical bibliography is a stage of alchemy; unexamined formulas are not yet knowledge.
entries.logic_practice: 1) For any cultivation recipe (herb, mineral, or ‘spiritual fire’ metaphor), demand lineage and earliest attestation. 2) Cross-read at least two independent witnesses before practice. 3) In BaZi remedial culture, reject one-off internet ‘elixirs’ lacking source chain. 4) Rank methods by transparency of process variables (times, signs, stop conditions). 5) Keep a rejected-formula list to prevent cyclic rediscovery of known dross.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with 石藥爾雅 (what the substance is called) and 大丹記 (how a great elixir proceeds), Jian Yuan answers ‘which text is trustworthy.’ It differs from hagiographic 神仙傳 by applying critical sourcing rather than faith in miracle stories; the why is risk control in a literature flooded with pseudepigrapha.

entries.logic_thesis: Da Dan Ji proves that the Great Elixir is a staged transformational sequence with observable phase-signs; success is recognized by correct transitions, not by duration alone. The record functions as a causal log: ingredients, fire, times, and endpoints form a reproducible argument.
entries.logic_chain: Premise: great elixir claims must be more than metaphor if they guide practice. → Inference: a 記 (record) structures process into ordered phases. → Inference: each phase has entry criteria and exit signs. → Inference: skipping phases or misreading signs collapses the product. → Conclusion: cultivation/alchemy is validated by matching lived signs to the recorded phase logic of the Great Elixir.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Translate the text’s stages into a checklist for neidan (or historical study for waidan): essence stabilization → qi movement → spirit condensation → resting. 2) Pair stages with BaZi periods: do not force late stages in years of severe Resource drain. 3) Define failure signs (agitation, insomnia, compulsive heat) as phase errors, not ‘tests from demons’ only. 4) Time stage shifts to monthly gua or solar terms per companion alchemical calendars. 5) Write your own 記 after each retreat—make personal causality as explicit as the classic.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 神仙養生祕術 (plural techniques for nurturing life) or 靈草歌 (herbal songs), Da Dan Ji centers one grand process model. It differs from purely philosophical 悟真篇 poetry by presenting record-like procedural logic; the why is to prove reproducibility of the ‘great’ work through staged evidence.

entries.logic_thesis: This text proves that immortality arts are composite: longevity emerges from a toolkit of secret techniques (breath, diet, sexual hygiene, herbs, exercises) coordinated as a system. No single trick substitutes for the full economy of nurturing life.
entries.logic_chain: Premise: body and spirit leak through multiple pathways. → Inference: each 祕術 patches a pathway (or optimizes a resource). → Inference: isolated practice leaves other leaks open, nullifying gains. → Inference: secrecy marks operational details that determine dose and timing. → Conclusion: true yangsheng is multi-factor control under disciplined sequencing, not one legendary method.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Audit your BaZi weak points (Blood/Resource, Officer stress, Output scatter) and assign a matching technique class from the book. 2) Build a daily stack: breath + sleep timing + diet restraint + mild movement. 3) Use ‘secret’ dosing logic—start minimal, increase only with stable pulse/sleep. 4) In sexual and emotional hygiene, treat Seven Killings months as high-leak periods. 5) Reassess quarterly; drop techniques that conflict (e.g. extreme sweating while yin is depleted).
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 大丹記’s single great-elixir arc, this is a modular secret-arts compendium. It differs from purely meditative 心性 texts by stressing somatic and dietary operations; the why is practical immortality as systems engineering of the living body.

entries.logic_thesis: The Spirit Herb Song proves that efficacious plants are knowable through mnemonic verse: morphological marks, habitats, and effects are compressed into song so field identification and use stay linked. Botanical correctitude is the hidden premise of ‘numinous’ results.
entries.logic_chain: Premise: wrong herb yields wrong or lethal effect. → Inference: oral-song form maximizes memorability for gatherers. → Inference: each stanza pairs appearance with function, encoding a mini argument. → Inference: ‘ling’ quality depends on true species plus right processing, not brand magic. → Conclusion: singing the herb is training the perceptual-logical map that makes spiritual pharmacy reliable.
entries.logic_practice: 1) When a BaZi remedy tradition names a grass/root, verify identity via the song’s traits before use. 2) Match herb natures (cold/hot, drying/moist) to chart excess-deficiency, not only to folklore prestige. 3) Use seasonal gathering cues in the verses as timing rules (parallel to month-gua discipline). 4) Prefer single-herb clarity before complex patent formulas. 5) Treat the song as exam material: if you cannot recite marks, you are not ready to dose.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 石藥爾雅 (mineral names) or abstract 丹經, this is field botany in poetic code. It differs from imperial Bencao encyclopedias by prioritizing portable song-logic for mountain practitioners; the why is operational memory under Baiyun immortal herb tradition rather than desk scholarship.

entries.logic_thesis: This mountain monograph proves that sacred geography is historical accumulation of adepts, rites, and sites: a mountain becomes ‘gold flower’ immortal terrain because lineage events sediment into landscape. Place is an archive of successful cultivation, not mute scenery.
entries.logic_chain: Premise: Chisong and related immortals leave traces in named peaks, caves, and shrines. → Inference: recording them as 志 binds story to coordinate. → Inference: later practitioners can navigate both terrain and method by the same map. → Inference: pilgrimage without the zhi is spatial tourism; with it, one enters a curriculum of place. → Conclusion: mountain gazetteers argue that Dao is locally proven—geography authenticates practice.
entries.logic_practice: 1) When selecting retreat sites, prefer places with documented immortal lineage over generic ‘pretty mountains.’ 2) Align personal BaZi travel stars and annual direction with the mountain’s historically potent sectors. 3) On-site, practice forms recorded in the zhi rather than imported unrelated systems. 4) Treat local taboos in the text as safety logic (spirit jurisdiction again). 5) After return, note which chart issues eased—build evidence for place-person fit.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike abstract 洞天記 lists, Jin Hua Chisong Shan Zhi is a thick local history of one range. It differs from pure 內傳 hagiography by grounding biography in topography; the why is to prove that cultivation success leaves mappable, revisit-able infrastructure.

entries.logic_thesis: Da Di Dongtian Ji proves that a Grotto-Heaven is an administrative-spiritual unit with boundaries, officers, and purification functions (‘great cleansing’). Entering it is changing legal-spiritual jurisdiction, which accelerates refinement when the adept respects the cave-heaven’s rules.
entries.logic_chain: Premise: Daoist cosmography ranks 洞天 as concentrated pure qi zones under specific governance. → Inference: Da Di’s record defines this zone’s identity and rites. → Inference: 滌 implies the locale’s primary causal gift is cleansing of turbidity. → Inference: correct entry timing and conduct open that function; violation closes it. → Conclusion: place-based cultivation works by jurisdictional immersion in a cleansing field, not by scenery psychology alone.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Schedule cave-heaven retreats during personal chart turbidity peaks (heavy combo of Direct Officer + Wet Earth, or illness pillars). 2) Observe entry purification from the记 before any ‘advanced’ practice. 3) Use shorter, repeated immersions if Day Master is weak—cleansing can feel draining. 4) Pair with confession chans so moral and qi turbidity clear together. 5) After exit, implement dietary/behavioral seals so re-pollution does not nullify the field effect.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with 赤松山志 (lineage-landscape history) or 王屋山聖跡記 (miracle traces), this text’s thesis is grotto-heaven as cleansing jurisdiction. It differs from generic fengshui ‘qi cave’ talk by embedding official Daoist dongtian administration; the why is canonical sacred geography rather than folk geomancy.

entries.logic_thesis: This record proves Wangwu’s Heavenly Altar as a site where imperial-celestial contact left verifiable ‘holy traces,’ so the mountain functions as a permanent interface for audience with higher powers. Pilgrimage and rite there borrow the residual authority of those traces.
entries.logic_chain: Premise: 聖跡 are material or narrative marks of successful theophany or immortal activity. → Inference: collecting them into a 記 creates an evidence portfolio for the site’s rank. → Inference: Wangwu as 天壇 implies altar-grade access, not ordinary scenic numen. → Inference: later ritual reenacts or plugs into that access channel. → Conclusion: practicing at Wangwu is argument by continuity—standing where heaven once answered multiplies the probability of response.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Reserve Wangwu (or analogous altar mountains) for petitions of rank: lifespan, ordination, major vow closure—not trivial wishes. 2) Read the聖跡 before ascent; ritually greet the specific traces named. 3) Choose years when BaZi Traveling Horse is active and beneficial. 4) Combine with Yuhuang or Shangqing chans that match the mountain’s historical pantheon. 5) Document personal ‘traces’ (events, dreams, recoveries) as continuation of the evidential logic.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 南嶽小錄’s broader Hengshan miscellany, this focuses on proving altar-grade sanctity via miracle inventory. It differs from 大滌洞天記’s cleansing-grotto thesis by emphasizing hierarchical audience (heaven’s altar) over purgation; the why is Wangwu’s classical status in retirement/immortal ascent lore.

entries.logic_thesis: Nan Yue Xiao Lu proves that a sacred marchmount is best known through compact, practical notes—temples, peaks, distances, numinous anecdotes—so the adept can orient without drowning in encyclopedism. Small-record form is an epistemology of usable sacred space.
entries.logic_chain: Premise: Nanyue is vast in cults and terrain. → Inference: without a concise lu, pilgrims misroute energy and time. → Inference: ‘small record’ selects operational facts over exhaustive history. → Inference: selection itself teaches what the tradition deems causally important. → Conclusion: effective mountain practice depends on a portable cognitive map of sites and their functions.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Before Nanyue pilgrimage, extract a route of sites matched to your aim (repentance temples vs. cultivation peaks). 2) Use the xiao lu’s scale notes to plan realistic day-qi expenditure for your constitution/chart. 3) At each stop, perform only the function historically noted—avoid ritual sprawl. 4) Compare your BaZi useful directions with the approach axes of major peaks. 5) After return, write your own ‘small record’ to refine future entries.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike long 山志 such as Chisong’s monograph, Xiao Lu prizes brevity and navigability. It differs from 聖跡記 by balancing logistics with lore rather than centering miracle proof; the why is handbook utility for the Southern Marchmount’s complex cult landscape.

entries.name_han: 太上玉清謝罪登真寶懺
entries.logic_thesis: This repentance proves that ascent to Zhen-hood (登真) is blocked by unconfessed faults against the Jade Clarity order; apology is the solvent of those blocks. Thus the path to perfection is not only refining qi but clearing legal-moral charges in the highest pure realm’s court.
entries.logic_chain: Premise: Yuqing is the apex purity stratum; its standards define true immortal rank. → Inference: offenses create incompatibility with that stratum. → Inference: 謝罪 is formal removal of incompatibility. → Inference: only then does 登真 become a coherent outcome of practice. → Conclusion: baochan links ethics and ontology—without apology, technical cultivation cannot seat in Jade Clarity.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Before attempting high neidan ‘spirit projection / immortal embryo’ stages, run full 謝罪 cycles. 2) Inventory faults against teacher, scriptures, body (jing waste), and beings—Yuqing logic is strict. 3) Time the chan in Metal/Water pure months or on your Authority days for solemnity. 4) Pair with silence retreat so apology is not immediately re-violated. 5) Treat recurring cultivation plateaus as possible unconfessed charges; audit again.
entries.logic_compare: Unlike 九幽拔罪 (rescuing beings from dark realms) or 泰清拔罪昇天 (Taiqing ascent after sin extraction), this text ties apology specifically to Yuqing-rank perfection. It differs from 宥罪錫福 (pardon for blessing) by aiming at ontological promotion (登真) rather than worldly fortune; the why is Shangqing/Yuqing soteriology of pure realization.

entries.name_han: 太上泰清拔罪昇天寶懺
entries.logic_thesis: This liturgy proves a two-stage causal law: extraction of sin (拔罪) must complete before heavenly ascent (昇天) can be authorized under the Taiqing dispensation. Ascent is not escape from judgment but the positive sequel of a cleared record.
entries.logic_chain: Premise: Taiqing governance handles salvation and aerial promotion of souls/practitioners. → Inference: residual guilt has weight that prevents rising. → Inference: chan systematically pulls out guilt (拔) rather than merely covering it. → Inference: 昇天 is the consequent state once weight is gone. → Conclusion: the ritual’s sequence is the argument—clear first, rise second—binding moral physics to celestial mobility.
entries.logic_practice: 1) Use for death anniversaries and for living practitioners stuck in ‘heavy’ chart years (strong Tomb storage, multiple punishments). 2) Never skip the 拔罪 half to rush ‘ascent’ visualizations—sequence is causal. 3) In BaZi terms, treat this as converting Killing/Officer pressure into pure Output rise only after confession. 4) Combine with merit transfer and precept renewal as ballast removal. 5) Indicators of success: lightness of mood-body, resolved nightmares, and opportunistic openings in career/cultivation path within weeks.
entries.logic_compare: Compared with 玉清謝罪登真, which emphasizes apology toward perfection in Jade Clarity, Taiqing 拔罪昇天 stresses extraction plus vertical lift under Taiqing. It differs from 九幽拔罪 by aiming upward to heaven rather than primarily liberating from underworld layers; the why is distinct bureaucratic heavens (Taiqing vs Yuqing vs Jiuyou) with different end-states: flight, zhen-hood, or underworld release.
